threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success metrics, and 30-day onboarding journey map.

messages.text: Good morning team. We're kicking off the hybrid onboarding program today. The goal is to design and roll out a standardized onboarding experience that works for both remote and on-site new hires within 21 days. We need to align on scope, define success metrics, and get the 30-day journey map approved. Let's start by confirming what we're building and what success looks like. Thoughts?

Thanks for the kickoff. I've already started thinking about the journey map structure. My sense is we should map out the first 30 days with clear touchpoints for day 1, week 1, week 2, week 3, and day 30. That gives us natural checkpoints for feedback and adjustment. I'm also thinking we need to be careful about information overload in week 1—the constraint says max 8 hours of training time, so we need to be selective about what's mandatory vs. optional. I can have a draft of A1 ready by end of day tomorrow if that works.

That timeline sounds good. Before we lock the journey map, I think we should run T1 first—the needs assessment with managers. That will tell us what gaps exist and what topics are actually critical. Otherwise we might design something that doesn't address real pain points. Can we schedule those interviews this week?

Good point. I'll own T1 and get those manager interviews scheduled by tomorrow. I'm thinking 5–7 managers across different departments so we get a real sense of what's missing. I'll summarize the findings and share them here before we finalize the journey map. That way the map is grounded in actual feedback.

I can help with scheduling if you need. Also, I'm wondering about the admin side—when do we need the checklist for contracts and payroll setup ready? I want to make sure I have time to coordinate with payroll on the system access piece.
Good question. T5 should be ready by day 10 so we have time to test it before the pilot. That gives you about a week and a half. Does that work with payroll's timeline?
I'll check with them. Should be okay but I'll confirm by end of week.

On success metrics—I think we should track completion rates, time-to-productivity for new hires, and satisfaction scores from both new hires and managers. We can pull those from the surveys at day 7 and day 30. That gives us early signals and a final assessment. I'd suggest we also track which modules are actually being used so we can refine for the next cohort. Should we define those metrics now or wait for the journey map to be finalized?

I think we can define the high-level metrics now and refine them once we see the journey map. The key is that we're measuring what matters—adoption, satisfaction, and actual impact on ramp-up time. I'll draft a short metrics framework and share it here for feedback.

I want to make sure we're clear on scope boundaries. Are we including role-specific onboarding modules or just core company-wide content? The risk note mentions that generic content might not be relevant to different departments. Should we plan for optional role-specific add-ons?

That's a smart question. I'd suggest we start with core mandatory content—company overview, policies, code of conduct, benefits basics—and then design the journey map to include optional slots for role-specific modules. That way managers can add department-specific training without overloading the core program. We can pilot with just the core content and add role-specific modules in phase 2 if needed.

I agree. Let's scope this to core mandatory content for the pilot. We can always expand. So to summarize where we are: T1 (needs assessment) starts this week, T2 (journey map) will incorporate those findings and be ready by end of week, and we'll define success metrics in parallel. Does everyone feel good about that direction?

Yes, that works. One thing I want to flag: we need to make sure the journey map includes clear compliance checkpoints. All HR policy and legal content needs to be reviewed before it goes live. I can do that review, but I want to make sure it's built into the timeline.
Absolutely. I'll flag compliance review as a gate in the journey map. Once the draft is ready, you'll review it before we finalize. That's built into the definition of done for T2.

Great. So we're aligned on scope: core mandatory content, optional role-specific modules for phase 2, and compliance review as a gate. That's D1 locked. For D2, we'll approve the journey map once T1 findings are in and T2 is drafted. I'll set a review checkpoint for Friday EOD. Everyone good?
Sounds good. I'll have the payroll confirmation by Friday too.
I'll have the metrics framework ready by Thursday so we can review it alongside the journey map.
Perfect. I'll have the journey map draft and T1 summary by Friday morning. Let's plan a quick sync Friday afternoon to review and finalize both D1 and D2.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize core training content and facilitator guide for live sessions.

messages.text: I've drafted the core onboarding training deck (A2) covering company overview, values, HR policies, and code of conduct. The deck is structured for a 90-minute live session with built-in interaction points. I'm also working on the facilitator guide (A6) which will include timing, key messages, and tips for keeping engagement high in a hybrid setting. Can you review the deck for compliance and clarity? I want to make sure the content is accurate and the tone works for both remote and on-site participants.

I'll review the deck for compliance. Can you share the link? I want to check the HR policies section especially—make sure we're aligned with current labour legislation and internal policies. How soon do you need feedback?

I'll upload it to the project folder and share the link by end of day. I'm hoping to get your feedback by Wednesday so I can incorporate any changes and finalize the facilitator guide by Thursday. Does that timeline work?
Yes, I can turn it around by Wednesday EOD.

Good move on the facilitator guide. One thing I want to confirm: what's the format for the live sessions? Are we doing one cohort session per week, or multiple sessions to accommodate time zones? And how many new hires per session? That will affect the interaction design.

Good question. I'm thinking we run one session per week, scheduled for a time that works for most time zones. We can record it for anyone who can't attend live. I'd cap it at 15 new hires per session to keep it interactive. If we get more than that in a cohort, we run two sessions. Does that feel right?

That works. One session per week, max 15 per session, recorded for async access. That's D4. Let me also flag: we need to make sure the facilitator guide includes tips for managing the hybrid dynamic—how to engage remote participants, when to use breakout rooms, etc. Can you build that into A6?

Absolutely. I'll include a section on hybrid facilitation best practices—camera expectations, chat monitoring, breakout room logistics, all of it. I'll also do a pilot run-through with you or someone from the team before we go live. That's part of the definition of done for T8.

One more thing on the deck: I want to make sure the code of conduct section is clear and actionable. New hires need to understand what's expected, not just read a policy. Can you include some real-world examples or scenarios?

Good idea. I'll add a few scenarios to the code of conduct section—things like how to handle conflicts, what to do if you witness something concerning, etc. That makes it more concrete. I'll include those in the draft I share today.

Perfect. So we're on track: deck draft today, compliance review by Wednesday, facilitator guide finalized by Thursday with hybrid best practices built in, and a pilot run-through before go-live. That covers D3 and D4. I'll confirm sign-off once I see the final versions.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on manager toolkit, HR admin checklist, and tracking process.

messages.text: I've drafted the manager onboarding toolkit (A3) which includes a checklist, sample 1:1 agenda, and a 30-day plan template. The idea is to give managers a simple, clear guide so they know what to do and when. I want to make sure it's practical and not overwhelming. Can you review it for clarity? Also, I want to align with you on the admin side—what does the HR assistant checklist (A4) need to cover, and how do we track completion (A5)?

I can review the toolkit for clarity and usability. From a trainer perspective, I want to make sure the 1:1 agenda includes time for the manager to explain the onboarding flow and set expectations. Managers often skip that step and new hires end up confused about what's coming next.

Good point. I'll make sure the first 1:1 agenda includes a section where the manager walks through the 30-day journey and explains what's mandatory vs. optional. That sets the tone and reduces confusion.

For the admin checklist, I'm thinking we need to cover: contracts and offer letter processing, payroll setup, system access requests, benefits enrollment, and mandatory forms like tax documents and emergency contacts. I'll draft that and get it to you by Wednesday. On tracking, I think we need a simple sheet that shows which new hire has completed what—modules, forms, system access, etc. Who should own updating that sheet?

That sounds comprehensive. On the tracking sheet, I think it should be a shared responsibility: you update it for admin items (contracts, payroll, system access), the trainer updates it for module completion, and managers update it for their 1:1s and check-ins. We can use a simple Google Sheet with color coding so it's easy to see at a glance what's done and what's pending.

That makes sense, but I want to make sure we're clear on who's responsible for what. Can we document that in the process description? I don't want things to fall through the cracks because everyone assumes someone else is updating it.

Absolutely. I'll create a process document that spells out exactly who updates what and when. That's part of T7. I'll also set up a weekly check-in where we review the tracking sheet together so we catch any gaps early.

I want to make sure the manager toolkit emphasizes the importance of the first week check-in. That's when we can catch issues early—if a new hire is confused or struggling, we want to know right away so we can adjust. Can you include a template for that check-in conversation?

Good idea. I'll add a first-week check-in template to the toolkit. It will include questions like: Are you clear on your role and responsibilities? Do you understand the onboarding flow? Are there any blockers or concerns? That gives managers a structured way to have that conversation.
I like that. And if the check-in reveals issues, we should have a clear escalation path. Who does the manager contact if a new hire is struggling? Is it HR, the trainer, or both?
Good question. I think the manager should contact HR first—either me or the HR assistant—and we'll coordinate with the trainer if needed. I'll include that in the toolkit and the process document.

I'll have the admin checklist draft ready by Wednesday. I'm also going to coordinate with payroll to make sure the system access timeline is realistic. I want to make sure we're not promising new hires access on day 1 if payroll needs 3 days to set things up.
Smart. Let me know what the realistic timeline is and we'll build that into the journey map and the toolkit. No point promising something we can't deliver.

Okay, so here's where we are: I'll finalize the manager toolkit (A3) with the first-week check-in template and escalation path by Thursday. You'll have the admin checklist (A4) by Wednesday. And I'll create the tracking process document (T7) with clear roles and responsibilities by Thursday. Once I have all three, I'll share them for final review. That covers D5 and D6.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in communication plan, FAQ, and rollout timeline for pilot.

messages.text: I've drafted the communication and FAQ pack (A8) for the new onboarding program. This includes key messages for managers, announcement templates for new hires, and a FAQ document covering common questions. The goal is to make sure everyone understands what's changing and why. I also want to lock in the pilot cohort, start date, and evaluation checkpoints. Can you review the communication plan and FAQ for completeness? And let's confirm the pilot timeline.

I'll review the FAQ for consistency with the training content. I want to make sure the answers align with what we're teaching in the onboarding sessions. Also, I'm thinking about the pilot cohort—how many new hires are we targeting? That will affect how we schedule the live sessions.

Good question. I'm thinking we target 10–15 new hires for the pilot. That's enough to test the program and get meaningful feedback, but small enough that we can manage any issues. Does that feel right?
That works. With 10–15 new hires, we can run one or two live sessions depending on timing. That's manageable. When are we thinking for the pilot start date?

I'm thinking we start the pilot on day 22 of the project—that gives us 21 days to build everything and do a final review. The pilot runs for 30 days, so we'll have feedback by day 52. That's tight but doable. We'll have evaluation checkpoints at day 7 and day 30 of the pilot to catch any issues early.

That timeline is aggressive but I think it's realistic if we stay focused. One thing I want to flag: we need to make sure the communication plan includes a message to managers about what we're asking them to do differently. Some managers might resist the new process if they don't understand the 'why' behind it.

Absolutely. I'll make sure the manager communication includes the business case—why we're standardizing, what problems we're solving, and what's in it for them. I'll also emphasize that we're asking for feedback during the pilot so we can refine based on their input.
I can help with the FAQ. I'm thinking we should include questions about the admin side—how long does system access take, when do I get my benefits info, etc. New hires always ask those questions.
Good idea. I'll add a section to the FAQ on admin and logistics questions. That way new hires have clear expectations about timelines and processes.
On the evaluation checkpoints—what are we actually measuring at day 7 and day 30? Are we using the surveys we defined earlier, or something else?

Yes, we're using the surveys from T6. At day 7, we'll send a quick pulse survey to new hires and their managers asking about clarity, relevance, and any blockers. At day 30, we'll do a more comprehensive survey plus informal check-ins to capture lessons learned. That feeds into T12—the pilot retrospective.
I want to make sure we also capture feedback on the live sessions specifically—what worked, what didn't, what should we change for the next cohort. I can include that in the day 7 and day 30 surveys.

Perfect. I'll make sure the surveys include specific questions about the live sessions and the overall onboarding experience. Okay, so here's the summary: pilot cohort is 10–15 new hires, starts day 22, runs for 30 days. Evaluation checkpoints at day 7 and day 30 using the surveys. Communication plan goes out before the pilot starts. That's D8. And D7 is the approval of the communication and FAQ pack. Can you all review those by Friday so we can finalize?
I'll review the communication plan by Friday. I want to make sure the messaging is clear and consistent across all audiences.
I'll review the FAQ by Friday EOD.
I'll review the admin section of the FAQ by Friday.

Great. I'll compile all the feedback and finalize the communication and FAQ pack by Friday EOD. Once that's approved, we're ready to move into execution mode. We'll have all the core materials ready by day 21, and the pilot starts day 22. Let's do a final readiness check on Friday afternoon before we launch.
